name: Schurch NDO
question: Does a single intradetrusor injection of onabotulinumtoxinA reduce incontinence in patients with neurogenic detrusor overactivity using intermittent catheterization?

design.population: Fifty-nine patients with urinary incontinence from neurogenic detrusor overactivity (53 with spinal cord injury and six with multiple sclerosis) required clean intermittent self-catheterization.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial; intent-to-treat diary analysis with mean imputation for missing primary values, two-sided α=0.05 and no multiplicity adjustment.
design.locator: Full text, Schurch 2005, Results, p 197; Full text, Schurch 2007, Methods, p 851

verdictNote: Between-group diary differences occurred at selected visits; no multiplicity adjustment.
takeaway: In 59 catheterizing patients with neurogenic detrusor overactivity, single intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 200 U or 300 U reduced daily incontinence episodes versus placebo at selected visits through 24 weeks; the 200-U comparison was significant at week 24.

reports.label: ICS/IUGA meeting abstract
reports.dateLocator: ICS/IUGA 2004 meeting dates, August 25-27; abstract publication day not stated
reports.citation: Schurch B, de Sèze M, Denys P, et al. "Botulinum toxin A (BOTOX) in neurogenic urinary incontinence: results from a multi-centre randomised, controlled trial." *ICS/IUGA Joint Meeting.* 2004;Abstract 151.
reports.noDoi: ICS meeting abstract 151 has no DOI or PMID; official abstract at https://www.ics.org/Abstracts/Publish/42/000151.pdf

harms.label: Autonomic dysreflexia and systemic events
harms.note: No autonomic dysreflexia or systemic events were observed; arm-specific counts were not reported.

delivery.label: Injection technique
delivery.value: Cystoscopic delivery as thirty 1-mL injections evenly across the detrusor, sparing the trigone.

reports.label: Initial efficacy and safety report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed citation and Crossref published-print: July 2005; exact day not stated
reports.citation: Schurch B, de Sèze M, Denys P, et al. "Botulinum toxin type a is a safe and effective treatment for neurogenic urinary incontinence: results of a single treatment, randomized, placebo controlled 6-month study." *J Urol.* 2005;174(1):196-200. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000162035.73977.1c

results.measure: Mean daily incontinence episodes: baseline and change at week 24; between-group ANOVA versus placebo at each visit

effect.p: 200 U vs placebo: 0.019 at week 24; 300 U vs placebo: 0.015 at week 2 and 0.047 at week 6

results.note: Between-group significance occurred only at the listed visits; no confidence intervals or multiplicity adjustment were reported.
results.locator: Full text, Results and Table 1, pp 197–198

results.endpoint: Incontinence Quality of Life total score
results.measure: Mean change from baseline and between-group comparison through week 24

values.b200: Improved from baseline at all visits (P ≤ 0.002); exceeded placebo at all visits
values.b300: Improved from baseline at all visits (P ≤ 0.002); exceeded placebo at all visits

results.note: The paper reports no numerical between-group estimate or confidence interval.
results.locator: Full text, Results, I-QOL and Fig 2, p 199

results.measure: At least one posttreatment diary week with no incontinence episodes
results.note: Placebo count is 29 total minus 24 active-treatment patients.

results.endpoint: Maximum detrusor pressure during bladder contraction
results.measure: Mean change from baseline at week 24, cm H₂O
results.note: Both active arms differed from placebo at week 24 (P < 0.05); no interval was reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Results, pp 198–199

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.locator: Full text, Safety results and Table 4, pp 198–199
harms.note: Among-group P=0.455; no adverse event was considered treatment-related.

harms.label: Injection pain, hematuria and serious adverse events

values.ctl: Injection pain 1/21; hematuria 0/21; serious skin ulcer 1/21

harms.note: Serious events were judged unrelated to treatment. No autonomic dysreflexia or systemic effects were seen. Clavien-Dindo grades were not reported.
harms.locator: Full text, Safety results and Table 4, pp 198–199

delivery.label: Injection and bladder management
delivery.value: Single 200-U or 300-U Botox dose, or saline placebo, in 30 mL total volume; thirty cystoscopic 1-mL intramuscular detrusor injections avoided the base and trigone. All patients performed regular clean intermittent self-catheterization.

delivery.label: Periprocedural care and treatment completion
delivery.value: Prophylactic antibiotics were administered. General anesthesia was used in 39.0%, local in 35.6%, spinal in 3.4%, and none in 22%. One 200-U-assigned patient withdrew before drug administration because of urethral stricture; another withdrew after week 6 for lack of efficacy.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, p 197

reports.label: Incontinence quality of life analysis
reports.citation: Schurch B, Denys P, Kozma CM, et al. "Botulinum toxin A improves the quality of life of patients with neurogenic urinary incontinence." *Eur Urol.* 2007;52(3):850-859. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2007.04.026

results.endpoint: Incontinence Quality of Life total score
results.measure: Median total I-QOL score among 56/59 patients with screening I-QOL; baseline and selected posttreatment scores on 0–100 scale

values.b200: Baseline 48.9; week 24 86.4; higher than placebo at every visit (P < 0.05)
values.b300: Baseline 44.3; week 6 77.3; week 24 67.0; higher than placebo at every visit (P < 0.05)

results.note: Intent-to-treat patients with screening I-QOL data were analyzed (56/59); arm-specific analyzed denominators and confidence intervals were not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, Fig 1, pp 851–852

results.endpoint: I-QOL psychosocial and social embarrassment subscales
results.measure: Median Psychosocial Impact and Social Embarrassment scores versus placebo at assessed visits

values.b200: Psychosocial Impact improved versus placebo at weeks 2, 6, 12 and 18; Social Embarrassment at weeks 6, 12, 18 and 24 (P < 0.05)
values.b300: Psychosocial Impact improved versus placebo at weeks 2, 6, 12 and 18; Social Embarrassment at weeks 6, 12 and 18 (P < 0.05)

results.locator: Full text, Abstract Results and Results sections 3.4–3.5, pp 851, 854–855

results.endpoint: Minimal important difference in total I-QOL

values.b200: Higher proportion than placebo at selected visits
values.b300: Higher proportion than placebo at selected visits

results.note: One or both active groups differed from placebo at all assessed visits except week 18; arm-specific numerator/denominator pairs were not printed.
results.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, Fig 1B, pp 851–853
